I am fifty-nine years old and have worked these fields in Quzhou County since I was a boy. I never went to school, but I know this land, the well water, and the seasons better than any words on paper. My family has about 15 mu. I will plant 12 mu with winter wheat and follow it with summer maize on the same ground after the June harvest, just as my father did. I will also keep 3 mu for cotton because the market price has been fair, though it needs more labor and spraying.

The wheat was already sown last October with my own saved seeds—about 30 jin per mu. Now, in spring, I will topdress it with urea and compound fertilizer and irrigate it three more times from the well before harvest. I rotary till before wheat sowing to loosen the soil. For the maize, I will buy hybrid seed packets—Denghai 605 or Nongda 372—from the village supply store. I will not till for maize; I sow directly into the wheat stubble to save fuel and time. The cotton needs rotary tillage in April, then sowing under plastic film. I fertilize with compound fertilizer as a basal dose and urea for topdressing, spreading by machine or hand. I spray for insects when I see aphids or worms—only a few times for the grains, but many times for cotton because the bollworms are stubborn. I irrigate by border flooding whenever the leaves start to curl.
